Prospective Doctoral Supervisor & Reviewer Summary

This statement synthesizes my research trajectory as a Research Assistant at Canterbury Christ Church University (CCCU), UK, bridging 10 accepted peer-reviewed publications, 3 forthcoming book chapters (Bentham Science), and ongoing 3D pancreatic CT segmentation research into an overarching doctoral agenda focused on trustworthy, clinically calibrated AI.

1. Overarching Research Vision

The translation of computer vision into clinical oncology remains bottlenecked by two persistent challenges: high false-alarm rates in boundary delineation of anatomically variable soft-tissue organs, and the opacity of high-capacity models that leaves clinicians unable to calibrate algorithmic risk.

My overarching research objective is to develop robust, explainable, and sample-efficient 3D deep learning architectures for medical volumetric imaging. Rather than treating organ segmentation as a generic dense prediction problem, my work investigates how domain-informed inductive biases—such as anatomical shape priors, multi-scale volumetric attention, and post-hoc attribution maps—can bridge the gap between benchmark benchmark metrics and bedside clinical trust.

Over the next 4–5 years, I aim to establish unified computational pipelines capable of simultaneously executing voxel-wise segmentation, uncertainty quantification, and interpretable clinical reasoning across multi-center abdominal CT cohorts.

2. Current Work: 3D Pancreatic CT Volumetric Analysis

[CURRENT FOCUS] Canterbury Christ Church University (2026 – Present)

Under my ongoing MSc Data Intelligence dissertation and Research Assistant placement at CCCU, I lead experiments on automated pancreatic parenchymal and lesion segmentation on abdominal contrast-enhanced CT scans.

The human pancreas poses one of the most demanding benchmarks in medical image analysis: it occupies less than 0.5% of total abdominal volume, exhibits high inter-patient morphological variation, and possesses Hounsfield Unit (HU) intensity distributions that overlap heavily with adjacent duodenum, stomach, and splenic vessels.

Key Methodological Interventions in Progress:

  • Hounsfield Unit (HU) Calibration: Implementing multi-window intensity normalization that preserves both soft-tissue parenchymal texture and vascular margins while suppressing extraneous pelvic and thoracic air/bone artifacts.
  • Hybrid CNN-Transformer Topologies: Investigating volumetric Swin-UNETR and hybrid 3D CNNs to capture both local voxel gradients (essential for irregular parenchymal boundaries) and global long-range contextual relationships across axial slices.
  • Class Imbalance Alleviation: Formulating customized Compound Loss objectives combining Soft Dice with Focal Cross-Entropy to penalize severe foreground-background voxel disparity without causing gradient saturation.

3. Methods & Methodological Strengths

My prior research across 10 peer-reviewed papers and 3 book chapters demonstrates a consistent methodology rooted in reproducible experimentation, rigorous ablation studies, and clinical explainability:

Explainable AI (XAI)

Specialized in gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM), Layer-CAM, and SHAP to ensure decision boundaries correlate with genuine pathology rather than image capture artifacts.

Compound Scaling & ViTs

Experience engineering tailored attention backbones (MobileNetV2-SA, EfficientNet, Vision Transformers) designed to maximize feature discrimination under restricted compute budgets.

Threshold Ensembles

Pioneered weighted threshold optimization and meta-stacking classifiers to improve diagnostic recall on high-stakes clinical disease cohorts (IEEE QPAIN 2026, ICECTE 2026).

Medical Data Pipelines

End-to-end fluency with DICOM / NIfTI formats, MONAI, SimpleITK, 3D Slicer, and PyTorch for reproducible 3D medical data loaders and augmentation pipelines.

4. Proposed Doctoral Research Directions

During doctoral study, I propose to explore three tightly coupled investigative tracks that extend my master's foundation:

  1. Uncertainty-Aware 3D Volumetric Segmentation:Developing Bayesian neural networks and test-time augmentation ensembling to produce spatial confidence maps alongside binary segmentation masks, signaling to radiologists where an automated boundary requires manual verification.
  2. Multi-Modal Cross-Attention Fusion:Integrating patient clinical metadata (demographic biomarkers, laboratory serum levels, staging records) with 3D radiological volumes via cross-modal attention transformers to refine borderline differential diagnoses.
  3. Federated and Privacy-Preserving Medical AI:Investigating parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) and federated averaging strategies to enable distributed model training across hospital networks without transmitting sensitive patient DICOM archives.

5. Motivation for Doctoral Research

My transition from core computer science at IUBAT (graduating with CGPA 3.84/4.00 and an IEEE ICCIT publication) to advanced Data Intelligence at Canterbury Christ Church University (averaging Distinction 70%) has reinforced my commitment to an academic research career.

A PhD will provide the dedicated intellectual environment and rigorous supervisory mentorship necessary to develop fundamentally novel AI architectures rather than merely adapting existing models. I look forward to joining a collaborative research lab where my strong work ethic, proven publication velocity (15 authored works spanning 2024–2026), and technical fluency in PyTorch and medical imaging can contribute immediately to ongoing funded grants.
